candidates.change_summary: Change returned AssertionPolicy to set blockAssertion = true instead of false.
Change returned AssertionPolicy to set arbitrateViaEscalationManager = true instead of false.
Change returned AssertionPolicy to set discardOracle = true instead of false.
Change returned AssertionPolicy to set validateDisputers = true instead of false.
Change returned AssertionPolicy to set all four fields to true instead of false.
Change constant true return to false so isDisputeAllowed always returns false.
Return value depends on whether assertionId is zero (false for zero, true otherwise) to alter behavior based on input.
Return value depends on whether disputeCaller is the zero address (false for zero address, true otherwise) to expose caller-based behavior change.
Replace empty body with a deterministic return of a nonzero price (1) instead of empty/no-return.
Replace empty body with a deterministic negative price return (-1).
Replace empty body with returning the time parameter cast to int256.
Replace empty body with returning keccak256(identifier) lower 32 bytes interpreted as int256 (may be negative), producing identifier-dependent value.
Add a state change by emitting the event then writing to a new public state variable requestPriceCounter incremented on each call (affects observable requestPrice())
Remove the require check so any caller can invoke functions guarded by onlyOptimisticAsserter, changing whether requestPrice() can be called and thus its observed state
Added a state-changing storage write that records the assertionId and assertedTruthfully into a public mapping when assertionResolvedCallback is called.
Make the onlyOptimisticAsserter modifier revert with a different message, changing observable revert behavior when called by a non-asserter.
Remove the onlyOptimisticAsserter modifier from assertionDisputedCallback so it can be called by any address, changing when assertionDisputedCallback can be invoked and thus its observed value.

Invert the require condition in onlyOptimisticAsserter so it reverts for the original optimistic asserter and allows all others, changing whether assertionDisputedCallback (which uses the modifier) can be called.
